sentences.text: This arthrodire placoderm possessed a wide head measuring roughly nine centimeters in length, featuring a brief, tapered nose.
Its overall look closely resembles that of the early selenosteid Pachyosteus.
Stensiö first described the genus in 1959 from remains located in the Late Devonian Kellwasserkalk facies of Bad Wildungen, Germany.
The original classification placed the animal in the single-species family Braunosteidae.
Later researchers moved it to Trematosteidae or Selenosteidae based on shared features like a postpineal fenestra and specific bone similarities.
Despite these changes, the Paleobiology Database currently lists its parent group as Braunosteidae within the class Placodermi.
Fossils of this creature date back to the Late Frasnian stage.
